standard_prerequisites.name: Universal property of set-quotients
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a set B, precomposition with q : A -> A/R is an equivalence between A/R -> B and the type of R-constant functions on A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement of the counted lemma is the assertion that the type of fixed points of r satisfies this same universal property, and the proof verifies it by exhibiting the equivalence of equation (6.10.?) directly.

standard_prerequisites.name: Paths in a sigma type over a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a set A, two elements (x,p) and (y,q) of Sigma x:A (r x = x) are equal as soon as x = y, and p and q need not be compared.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the comparisons at source lines 1343, 1356 and 1361 harmless, since B is a set and the second components are propositions.

core_obligations: Introduce i : prd x:A r(r x) = r x witnessing idempotence of r and define q : A -> (A/R) by q(x) := (r(x), i(x)) (source lines 1341-1342).
Show that q(x) = q(y) if and only if r(x) = r(y), hence by hypothesis if and only if x `eqr` y, using that A is a set (source line 1343).

Define the map e from left to right in the displayed equivalence by e(f) := (f o q, _), where the second component transports x `eqr` y to f(q x) = f(q y) using the previous step (source lines 1344-1347).
Define the candidate inverse e'(g,s)(x,p) := g(x) and compute e'(e(f))(x,p) = f(q(x)) = f(r(x),i(x)) = f(x,p), the last equality because p : r(x) = x and A is a set (source lines 1348-1356).

Compute the other round trip e(e'(g,s)) = (g o proj1 o q, _), observe that the second component needs no attention because B is a set, and identify g(proj1(q x)) = g(r x) = g(x) using r(x) `eqr` x and the hypothesis s that g respects the relation (source lines 1357-1367).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the canonical map q out of the idempotent and relate q(x) = q(y) to r(x) = r(y) and to the relation.
Build the forward map e of the universal-property equivalence.
First round trip, where the fixed-point equation p : r(x) = x is consumed.
Second round trip, where the set-ness of B discards the coherence component and the hypothesis s identifies g(r x) with g(x).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.10.8 at source lines 1321-1338: if A is a set, r : A -> A is idempotent and (r x = r y) is equivalent to x `eqr` y, then the type of fixed points of r satisfies the universal property of the quotient of A by `eqr`. The statement is long and its proof (source lines 1340-1368) is a full quasi-inverse construction, not a corollary of the general quotient theory: the map q(x) := (r(x), i(x)) is built from a witness of idempotence (lines 1341-1342), the equivalence e/e' has to be written down explicitly (lines 1344-1350), and both round trips depend on separate facts, the first on the fixed-point equation p : r(x) = x together with A being a set (line 1356) and the second on B being a set to discard the coherence component plus the hypothesis s to replace g(r x) by g(x) (lines 1361-1367).
